correctness.rationale: For every frame, one simplex has cube-fitting radius half the largest coordinate prefix range. Over permutations this range equals max of the positive and negative row totals. Integer full-rank matrices have nonzero rows, giving minimum at least 1/2, with equality precisely for rows ±e_j or e_j−e_k. These rows are a reduced oriented edge incidence matrix of a graph on d+1 vertices, invertible iff it is a tree. Leaf expansion proves determinant ±1; Prüfer coding plus edge labels and orientations gives exactly 2^d(d+1)^(d−1) unordered frames. Exact verifier enumerates all threshold-admissible d×d matrices for d≤4 and every row in {-2,-1,0,1,2}^d for d≤5. The proof, not these tests, establishes the unbounded-dimensional statement.

originality.rationale: The newly proved contribution is the complete structure and exact cardinality of all cube-optimal common frames, not the previously known radius. Primary full-text comparisons find the optimal-value formula and one-simplex fitting conditions but not the all-frame incidence-tree classification. Numerous exact semantic queries and inspected historical claims revealed no statement implying this enumerator. The classical spanning-tree and total-unimodularity ingredients are acknowledged. Residual historical priority risk remains because search cannot establish global uniqueness.
residual_risks: A previous treatment of optimizers of unit-cube Kuhn triangulations under other terminology (especially signed incidence matrices or integer polyhedral coverings) may imply the result, despite no matching source in the actual searches.

The Prüfer enumeration and the unimodularity of tree incidence matrices are classical, so the originality claim is restricted to their exact role as the optimizer classification for the newly defined packet radius.
No independent expert or exhaustive historical-priority audit was performed.

value.rationale: The complete optimizer family for the natural cube benchmark of the newly introduced common-frame covering invariant has a nonobvious graph-theoretic classification: oriented labeled spanning trees, basis rigidity despite allowing sublattices, and an exact all-dimensional optimizer count. This answers the equality/multiplicity question left open by a mere radius calculation and supplies a useful canonical comparison for future shape/lattice perturbations; the object and invariant are natural, rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
